comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Observed in use on 0.4.1, which is the evidence this card said it was waiting for.

Driving a laptop and a devenv in one window, I wanted the local side gone for the day and to work on the devenv alone. Closing the local pane three times produced a fresh local tab and pane each time, with a new id every round:

    t206zcc903 / p206zc68fg  ->  closed
    t206zpgpw6 / p206zpeagf  ->  closed
    t206zwkf92 / p206zwsnkx  ->  and so on

The workaround the card predicted is the one I had to use: take the `[[daemon]]` block out of `~/.muster/config.toml`. `muster reload` does not apply it either - `daemons_differ` logs "relaunch to pick up a `[[daemon]]` change" - so it also costs a relaunch, and with it every pane in the window.

Two things the card did not anticipate.

It was the **local** machine I wanted empty, not the remote one. The card reasons about a devenv shell appearing over ssh, but wanting one machine off screen has nothing to do with which machine it is: I was working on the devenv and the laptop half was in the way.

And **there is no way to ask for this short of the config**. `muster pane close` is the only verb that empties a machine, and it is the trigger for refilling it. So the answer to "I am done with this machine for now" is to edit a file and relaunch, which loses the state of the machine you are keeping.

That moves me to the card's first option - ask once per attach, and leave a machine empty once you empty it - now that `muster pane new --daemon <id>` exists as the way back. The property given up is that the window can show a machine holding nothing you cannot use, and the sidebar heading already says `no tabs, so this daemon is holding nothing`, so that state is visible rather than silent.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Answered, though not yet built. The 2026-09-01 comment settled on the card's first option - ask once per attach, and leave a machine empty once you empty it - and the reason it is still open is that the rule it wants deleted is the same rule the tab model deletes.

`open_remaining_regions` refills a machine because the window is a column per machine: a machine with no region has nothing on screen, and a window showing a machine you cannot use is the state `a_2HpkpfIfq` was about. Once a window holds an ordered list of Muster tabs with one on screen (MIP-2, stages three and four, carded as `a_2IoXIHzri`), nothing is owed a column and the rule stops existing in its present form. Deleting it before then would put back the hole `a_2HpkpfIfq` closed.

So this card's answer is: yes, refilling is too eager, and it goes when the tab model does. MIP-2 says so in "What gets easier". Moving it to `backlog-hi` rather than leaving it in `uncommitted`, because the question is settled and only the sequencing is outstanding.

One thing the 2026-09-01 comment turned up that outlives the rule and is worth keeping in view: `muster reload` does not apply a `[[daemon]]` change, so detaching a machine costs a relaunch and every pane in the window with it. That is a separate gap from refilling and stays one after the tab model lands.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Closing the last pane on a machine now gets you a fresh shell on it, because the window asks any attached machine that says it holds nothing for a workspace (`a_2HpkpfIfq`). That closed a real hole: before it, a machine reaching zero panes dropped out of the window's reach entirely, and the only way back was `herdr workspace create` or editing the saved arrangement.

The question is whether the rule is too eager now that it runs per machine rather than per window.

`open_a_workspace_if_the_window_is_empty` has always refilled a window with no panes at all, and nobody has objected to that: a window showing nothing is not a state anybody wants. Applied per machine, the same rule means closing the devenv's last pane spawns a devenv shell, over ssh, a moment later. Somebody who has finished with a machine for the afternoon cannot stop it holding a pane without taking its `[[daemon]]` block out of the config and relaunching.

Not observed as a complaint - raised from reading the change rather than from using it, which is the honest provenance and also the reason to wait. What would settle it is driving a two-machine window for a day and noticing whether a devenv shell you did not ask for ever gets in the way.

Things that might be true if it does:

- **Ask once per attach rather than whenever a machine empties.** A machine gets its first pane and is then left alone; closing the last one leaves it empty and reachable through `muster pane new --daemon <id>`, which now exists. Cheapest, and it gives up the property that the window is never showing a machine you cannot use.
- **Ask for the local machine and offer for a remote one.** A row in the agent list that opens a pane on an empty machine, rather than one appearing. That is the sidebar affordance `a_2HpkpfIfq` deliberately deferred, and it depends on the tab model `docs/mip/0002-muster-tabs.md` is about.
- **A setting.** Last resort - this is a question about what Muster is for, and a key that lets both answers exist is how you avoid deciding.
- **Leave it.** A machine you are not using is one you take out of the config, and a pane costs a shell.
title: 🌱 Is refilling a machine that empties too eager?
